newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks ease by lunch on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks ease by lunch on profit taking.

text.p: Thai stocks eased by lunch on Tuesday on profit taking after sharp technical rebounds in the past two sessions but investors sold finance stocks on renewed concern over the quality of their assets, traders said.
The SET Index lost 0.28 points, or 0.06 percent, to 504.25 by the break. The SET 50 rose 0.19 points, or 0.53 percent, to 36.07 on trade worth 2.53 billion baht.

Investors continued buying selected blue-chips but others were anxious to take gains ahead of a Tuesday cabinet meeting, a parliamentary budget debate on Wednesday, and economic data being released on Thursday, traders said.
The index rallied 5.06 percent on Monday.

"I think there is some profit taking. We are all very interested in the budget...there is this talk about finance mergers but I think we'll have to wait for action to be implemented," said a trader at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
"We are also anxious to see the figures on Thursday...the main thing we'll be looking for is foreign reserves," he added.

A Thai finance company executive on Monday estimated non-performing loans in the finance sector at as high as 31.5 percent of its total loans. His comment and tight liquidity helped wipe 4.09 percent off finance stocks, brokers said.
Speculative and foreign fund buying centred on communications and selected banks shares.

Telecommunications conglomerate United Communication Indutry added 6.50 baht to 104, mobile phone firm Advanced Info Service rose 13 to 170, and Industrial Fiannce Corp of Thailand gained 2.25 to 30.50.
